newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euris said not ruling out Casino alliance.
newsitem.headline: Euris said not ruling out Casino alliance.

text.p: French holding group Euris, which has 33 percent of Casino, did not rule out an alliance by the food retailer with another food stores group such as Promodes, newspaper Les Echos said in a report to appear on Tuesday.

Asked by Les Echos whether he would exclude an alliance, Euris chairman Jean Charles Naouri replied, "No, certainly not, neither with Promodes nor with others but the principle of an alliance is not an obligation."
"Paul-Louis Halley (chairman of Promodes)...outlines perspectives which, among others, should be part of our strategic reflections," he added.

Shares in Casino rose sharply earlier this month after Halley forecast consolidation in the French food retail sector. He raised the idea that Promodes could ally with another retailer and did not reject the possibility it might be with Casino.
However, Naouri also said Casino had the capacity to develop independently. "Size is certainly a pertinent aspect but not the only one. Other approaches are possible such as specialisation," he said.
The priority for the moment, he said, was to continue improving management of Casino. "The company's results ...can still improve significantly," he said.
Casino reported in September that its 1996 half-year net profit rose 44.8 percent to 294 million francs.
Retail analysts have said Casino might be an ideal match for Promodes. A merger of the two would create the biggest French food retailer with 18.4 percent of the market.
